chapter: Black and Tan and Kansas City nightlife
title: Singing with Count Basie's band at the Black and Tan
summary: White patrons came to hear The Singin' Bartender; Basie's band played for him and he walked the aisles collecting tips.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: So, then, we run...we run the place a lo-o-o-ong time. We had all the bigshots from downtown comin' over there. We have a balcony full of white folks. They come to the Black and Tan...to hear The Singin' Bartender sing. I'd make money hand-over-fist...a lot of tips...put 'em all in a...I'd be in the...the band's in the balcony, and I'd get out behind the bar, go up the steps, an' Count Basie and them'd play for me. I'd sing, and then I'd...I have a strong voice...I'd leave the bandstand and walk around through the aisles and sing. Pick up the money. That was the highlight of the evenin'--singin' and pickin' up the bread.
How big a band did Basie have then?
Yeah, he had a big band.
Ohhhh, Herschel Evans...Sammy Price...Ben Webster...oh, a whole lotta people. Some of them...he got one or two of them boys still workin' with 'im...workin' with all...workin' all this time...
Yeah, they ain't stopped. They been in...they with him a long time. The guitar player with Count Basie--he's there.
He been with him for years. Years and years and years.
